title: Fresh Blood
paragraphs: Now then, to protect Father and the others, I shall wipe out everything in my path!
“Aiming Lancer X! Brionac X!”
I raised my spear high—though I had to adjust for the ceiling—before systematically taking down the surrounding soldiers. For the crime of falsely accusing Father, I will make them pay.
“Guaaaaaaah!?”
“Uwaaaaaaaah!?”
“Wh-why… wasn’t he supposed to be low-level…?”
“Th-this is… the strength of an Otherworlder…?”
The soldiers were each gasping out their dying words. Too late now. Learn from your own foolishness.
“Die, fake Hero! Haaaaaah!”
One knight, who had somehow managed to dodge, lunged at me. He could still move, but he was far too weak to take on a Hero.
“Your movements are slow and pathetic.”
I didn’t even need to use a skill—just thrust my spear straight into his chest.
The knight, now impaled, stared at me in shock, his gaze shifting between my spear and his own chest. How ridiculous.
“If you wish to die, then by all means, step forward.”
I swung my spear, flinging the knight’s body away. Ah, some of his blood splattered onto Ren and Itsuki’s faces. It made a nice splat sound.
“Hii!?”
“Ah…”
Ren and Itsuki went pale. They touched their cheeks, staring at the fresh blood on their hands.
“W-we had no choice… They tried to kill us first…”
“Y-yeah. We have to defend ourselves… This is war. When people die, of course… there’s blood…”
“Awaawa…”

Father and the others were stunned at how quickly everything had unfolded. Ah, I see. They still weren’t used to battle. Even when fighting monsters, blood is spilled when you cut them down. Ren, Itsuki, and Father simply hadn’t come to terms with that yet. It’s fine to reflect on it later, but right now, the priority is dealing with Trash and the crimson swine. I had aimed for them, but they managed to evade. Or rather, the knights and soldiers got in the way. …No, that’s not it. The crimson swine had used the knights as shields. What a despicable creature.
“Bububububuhii! Buhii!”
The crimson swine, realizing the tide had turned, tried to flee. I won’t let you. If I let you escape now, it will only sow the seeds of future chaos.
“Where do you think you’re going?”
I swiftly pursued and skewered it.
“M-Malty!”
Trash, frozen in terror, cried out for the crimson swine.
“This makes three times now. Begone!”
“Burst Lance X!”
I detonated the tip of my spear, obliterating the crimson swine in an instant. At full power, not even a scrap of flesh remained—only ashes.
“Maltieeeeeeeeeee!”
Trash let out a scream.
“Unforgivable! I won’t forgive you! How dare you—damn you fake Heroes!”
Trash glared at us, seething with rage like an inferno.
Fake? Are you seriously claiming that we’re the fakes when you’re the ones losing to us?
“You brought this upon yourself. If you had simply let us go, none of this would have happened. In fact, you should be grateful—we just rid the world of its worst poison.”
If I recall correctly…
Trash had ended up cooperating in taking down the crimson swine in the end. But in exchange for saving Father and the others, any possibility of reconciliation had been completely shattered.
“I will make sure you die a slow and miserable death! Soldiers! Get in here, now!”
Why doesn’t he fight for himself? He’s supposed to be the Staff Hero, so why isn’t he fighting anymore? I vaguely remember that, in the first world, he actually did battle.
“Even now, you’re relying on others? If you want to run, now is your chance.”
“Shut up! Dieeeeeeeeeeeeeee!”
Trash foolishly raised his fist and lunged at me.
Pathetic. The so-called “Wise King of Wisdom” is nothing but a delusion.
“Time for a spectacular demise! Brionac X!”
“Guaaah—”
Trash took a direct hit from my Brionac and was completely obliterated. Not even a trace of him remained.

Oh? Light gathered where he had been and shot off somewhere. Looking around, the only ones still standing were Father and the others. Everyone else was either dead or gravely wounded—the entire area was a sea of corpses. Last time, Father had said something like, “There might be some trouble, but just find a way to escape.”
Well, we did it! A flawless victory!
Huh? The Father in my memories is scolding me, “Who told you to kill everyone?!” Must be my imagination. I’m sure he’ll praise me.
“E-even if we were in the right… this is…”
“This is what happens in battle. When you defeat the enemy, this is the result…”
“Ugh… So many people just died right in front of us…”
Father and the others still weren’t used to bloodshed.
“Hurry! Kill the fake Heroes!”
The castle was growing restless. Even with their leader, Trash, dead, the kingdom’s soldiers weren’t giving up. At this rate, Father and the others will be in danger.
“This smell… this sensation…”

“Yeah… This is our reality. A dream-like fantasy of another world… but in the end, ‘justice triumphing over evil’ just means taking someone’s life… We never should have let ourselves get excited about this…”
“Yeah… I thought, ‘they should all just die,’ but seeing them actually die… it’s so… real…”

Father and the others seem pretty down. Well, I suppose it’s natural. When I first killed a monster that looked more like a living creature, I also felt some resistance. They’ll gradually get used to it.
“Shall we show them what happens when they defy a Hero?”
“Y-you’re going to do even more!?”
“Isn’t this enough!? If we go too far, we won’t even know who’s right anymore!”
“Exactly!”
Father and the others are hesitating. Oh well. I’ll just use a portal— Ah, I just remembered.
Éclair. If we leave her behind, she’ll definitely die.
“Before we escape, there’s one more person we need to rescue.”
“What!? You’re going back now!?”
“Why didn’t you say so sooner!?”
“If we don’t, she’ll die.”
“You’re saying this after massacring all these people!?”
“Who is it?”
I tilted my head, and Father and the others started discussing among themselves. Somehow, it reminds me of Father and the sisters from the first world.
“I guess it’s like… no mercy for enemies, but allies get saved?”
“Maybe. I mean, to escape this place, we didn’t really have a choice.”
“If this were a game, we’d probably just kill everyone here. Any NPCs tied to the story would just escape on their own.”
“In Dimension Wave, the event outcome changes based on your actions. But… this isn’t a game. If it were, this level of realism would be insane…”
“No, at this point, even if this was a game, we can’t afford to act carelessly.”
“What’s wrong?”

Father and the others cautiously turned their gazes toward me. If we don’t hurry, the soldiers will swarm in. Ah, I’ve got an idea. I’ll create a wall of fire along the path leading to the throne room. A blazing barrier that lets nothing through. The soldiers won’t even be able to get close. While I cast the spell, I’ll buy time for Father and the others to finish their discussion.
“Do we really have to save this person?”
“I promised in the previous loop. Besides… she’s definitely trustworthy.”

Back in the second-to-last loop, she helped escort Father to Siltvelt. And during the war, she played an active role in stopping the fighting. She’s from a respectable background, and she’s serious. If we explain the situation, she’ll definitely come with us.
“Even so…”
“Don’t worry, it won’t take long.”
“You say that so lightly… Um, is there any way to do this with as few casualties as possible?”
Father asked me that with a pleading expression.
Hmm. Since it’s a request from Father, I suppose I should consider if it’s possible.
“It’s not impossible, but it might put you all in danger.”
“I still want to ask. You’re strong, aren’t you?”
Looks like Ren, Itsuki, and Father finally understand my strength.
Since I’ve been entrusted with this, I, Motoyasu, will accomplish it—no matter what!
“Understood. From here on, I’ll make sure all enemies are only incapacitated.”
“Please!”
Father and the others still seem a little scared. But there’s no helping that.
